labels.label: bzdef:c3s2d1_somme_convexes
labels.notes: IsSommeConvexes = Convex W, every V i convex, and p = sum is an IsIsoConvexes from univ.pi V onto W (BijOn, and p and invFunOn p preserve two-point convex combinations). Fintype I with I empty allowed, any real vector space. isSommeConvexes_iff_bijOn proves it is exactly 'V i convex and p a bijection onto W' (W's convexity follows by linear image), so any reading of « isomorphisme ... pour les structures affines » from 'bijection' to 'affine bijection with affine inverse' gives the same notion. Reading that does no harm, as the dispatch said. composante_spec gives the components. The mark on a definition is honest.

labels.label: bzrem:c3s2r1_somme_classes
labels.notes: Unmarked and partial, which is correct. KE E = {s // Convex ℝ s} includes ∅. That matches the paper: Ch. 1 l.269–271 defines K(E) as « l'ensemble des parties convexes » with no nonemptiness, and Ch. 3 Déf. 5 (l.557) uses « le convexe vide » explicitly in a sum. KModE is the orbit quotient and SommeClasses is the paper's definition. remarque1_somme_unique is the first assertion as printed (∃!). remarque1_famille adds [Nonempty I]. remarque1_infinite adds two distinct indices, Nontrivial E and W' nonempty. Both additions are disclosed. I checked the counterexamples. not_remarque1_famille_fin_zero: for Fin 0 the only product point sums to 0, so {0} is the sum, the class of {1} is the class of {0}, and no empty family sums to {1}. Valid. not_remarque1_infinite_vide: the class of ∅ is {∅}, the product is empty and BijOn onto ∅ holds, so exactly one family. Valid. The E = 0 case is argued but not formalized (K(0) = {∅,{0}}, each class a singleton) and is correct. See findings for how this should be worded.

labels.label: bzprop:c3s2p1_decomposition_origine
labels.notes: The hypotheses are SommeClasses w v (= « ∑ v_i = w » in Remarque 1's sense), W of class w, and 0 ∈ W. The conclusion is ∃! system V with classes v i, 0 ∈ V i and IsSommeConvexes W V. Nothing is added, and any finite I is allowed (n = 0 holds too, since then W = {0}). The gap is filled correctly. In the printed proof the claim that the V'_i − x'_i are the only systems is unargued. subset_of_translate_somme proves U_i ⊆ V_i from the BijOn of V, MapsTo of U, U_i = a_i + V_i and 0 ∈ U_i, using a midpoint comparison of two decompositions of y/2 and injectivity. It is applied in both directions to get equality. The finding is accurately described as a missing step, not an error in the statement. The mark is honest.

labels.label: bzrem:c3s2r2_somme_infinie
labels.notes: Unmarked and partial, which is correct. IsSommeInfinieTexte formalizes the wording: convex, contains 0, and every x ∈ W with x ≠ 0 has a unique finitely supported family with components in V_i and sum x. IsSommeInfinie is the reading: BijOn of sommeF from {f | ∀ i, f i ∈ V i} onto W. isSommeInfinie_iff_texte shows the reading is exactly the wording plus MapsTo (the x = 0 case is derived). isSommeInfinie_iff_isSommeConvexes shows it agrees with Déf. 1 for finite I. The finding is sound: W = [0,1], V = [0,2] with one index meets the wording and fails Déf. 1 (isSommeInfinieTexte_not_isSommeConvexes, checked). See the minor finding on the possible reading of « (x ≠ 0) »; the finding holds under that reading too.

labels.label: bzrem:c3s2r3_somme_directe
labels.notes: remarque3_somme_directe: for Fintype I, IsSommeConvexes univ (Ei) ↔ DirectSum.IsInternal Ei. That is both the paper's implication and its « coïncide » sentence. The theorem is also proved for any subspace W (remarque3), which is more general than the paper, so Lean ≥ paper. The infinite-I version holds in both the reading (remarque3_somme_directe_infinie) and the literal wording (remarque3_somme_directe_texte) of Remarque 2, so the mark does not depend on Remarque 2's reading. Honest.

findings.what: Remarque 1 is characterized as « false as printed » in degenerate cases. The counterexamples are correct, and the empty-set one is inside Benzécri's own conventions: K(E) is all convex parts (Ch. 1 l.269–271), and Ch. 3 Déf. 5 l.557 uses the empty convex. So the clause does fail literally. But all three failures are boundary omissions (n = 0, W' = ∅, E = 0), not a mathematical error in the remark. An author-facing register entry should read « imprecise: the second assertion needs n ≥ 1; the infinitude needs n ≥ 2 (with n ≥ 1, n ≠ 1), W' ≠ ∅ and E ≠ 0 », not « false ». The E = 0 case is argued and not formalized, so it must be labelled as argued wherever it is cited.
findings.fix: When /restate registers it, use the 'imprecise' wording above. Keep the not_ names (not_remarque1_famille_fin_zero, not_remarque1_infinite_vide): they are genuine refutations of the literal clause, and they are what restate.py keys on. The rewritten statement should be anchored on remarque1_famille / remarque1_infinite.

findings.what: « x = Σ_{i∈N} x_i (x ≠ 0) » may instead mean that the terms x_i are nonzero (N is the support, which makes « d'une façon et d'une seule » meaningful for a finite sum), rather than that the point x is nonzero. The Finsupp formalization covers both: uniqueness of the finitely supported family is uniqueness of its support and terms, and the x = 0 case is derived in isSommeInfinie_iff_texte. So the finding that the wording omits that every finite sum of components lies in W is sound under either reading. SCOPE names only one reading.
findings.fix: Add one sentence to SCOPE saying that « (x ≠ 0) » may qualify the terms x_i, and that the finding and the reading are unchanged under that reading.
